entry: American actor, director and producer. Robbins took supporting roles in *The Sure Thing* (1985), *Top Gun* (1986) and *Bull Durham* (1988) before leading roles in *Jacob's Ladder* (1990), *The Player* (1992) and *The Shawshank Redemption* (1994). He won an Academy Award for *Mystic River* (2003), directed by [[Clint Eastwood]], and his direction of *Dead Man Walking* (1995) earned an Academy Award nomination for Best Director. He is known for political activism, including opposition to the [[Iraq War]].

City in Mali, capital of the Tombouctou Region, about 20 km north of the Niger River (pop., 2023: about 84,000). Timbuktu became a permanent settlement early in the 12th century and flourished on trans-Saharan trade in salt, gold and ivory after a visit by [[Mansa Musa]] around 1325. It became part of the [[Mali Empire]] in the early 14th century and was absorbed by the [[Songhai Empire]] in 1468. A Moroccan army defeated the Songhai in 1591 and made the city its capital. Timbuktu's Islamic scholars and the Sankoré Madrasah, an Islamic university, made it a scholarly center in Africa, supported by an important book trade. After its golden age came decline, and France took over Mali in 1893. Timbuktu was designated a [[World Heritage Site]] in 1988 for its mud-brick mosques. Extremist groups later destroyed cultural sites, but local efforts preserved much of its manuscript collection.

Difference in elapsed time between two clocks, caused by [[Velocity|relative velocity]] or by a difference in gravitational potential. [[Special relativity]] predicts that a clock moving relative to an observer ticks more slowly, and [[Albert Einstein]] showed in 1905 that the effect concerns the nature of time itself. The faster the relative velocity, the greater the dilation, with time slowing to a stop as a clock approaches the [[Speed of light|speed of light]]. Predictions have been repeatedly confirmed by experiment, and the effect is of practical concern in [[Satellite navigation]] systems such as the [[Global Positioning System]].

American weekly news magazine based in [[New York City]]. Published weekly for nearly a century, it has appeared every other week since March 2020. Time was first published on March 3, 1923, by Briton Hadden and Henry Luce, and was the first weekly news magazine in the United States. Its co-founder Henry Luce ran it for many years after Hadden's death in 1929. Until the late 1960s its covers showed a single person, and more recently it has published "People of the Year" issues. A European edition is published in [[London]], an Asian edition in [[Hong Kong]], and a South Pacific edition in [[Sydney]]. Since 2018 the magazine has been owned by Salesforce founder Marc Benioff, who acquired it from Meredith Corporation.

Hypothetical travel into the past or future. The idea of a time machine was popularized by [[H. G. Wells]]'s 1895 novel *The Time Machine*, and the concept appears in philosophy, physics and fiction, particularly [[Science fiction]]. Forward time travel is an observed phenomenon through [[Time dilation|time dilation]] and is well understood within special and [[General relativity]]. Making one body advance or delay more than a few milliseconds relative to another is not feasible with current technology. Whether travel to the past is physically possible is uncertain, and it may raise questions of causality. Some solutions of general relativity allow it, such as a rotating black hole, but travel to an arbitrary point in spacetime has limited support and is usually linked to [[Quantum mechanics]] or wormholes. One early example of backward time travel is the Chinese novel *A Supplement to the Journey to the West* (c. 1640), in which [[Sun Wukong]] travels back to the [[Qin dynasty]] and forward to the [[Song dynasty]].

Area that observes a uniform standard time for legal, commercial and social purposes. Time zones tend to follow national borders rather than strict [[Longitude]]. Each is defined by an offset from [[Coordinated Universal Time]] (UTC), ranging from UTC−12:00 to UTC+14:00. Most offsets are whole hours, but some, such as those in [[India]] and Nepal, differ by 30 or 45 minutes. Many areas use [[Daylight saving time]] in spring and summer, one hour ahead. Each place once kept its own solar time, which varies by about four minutes for each degree of longitude. The Royal Observatory at Greenwich, founded in 1675, established [[Greenwich Mean Time]] (GMT) as a standard reference for mariners. The Great Western Railway began using GMT in 1840, and North American railroads implemented four continental zones on November 18, 1883.

Scientific projections of far-future events, from 3001 CE onward. Predictions draw on astrophysics, particle physics, evolutionary biology, plate tectonics and sociology. All projections must account for the [[Second law of thermodynamics]], under which entropy rises over time. The Sun will likely expand enough to overwhelm [[Mercury (planet)|Mercury]], [[Venus]] and possibly Earth, then shrink to the size of a [[White dwarf]]. Long afterward, physicists expect matter itself to disintegrate through radioactive decay. Five spacecraft, including [[Voyager 1]], [[Voyager 2]] and [[New Horizons]], are on trajectories out of the Solar System and should persist indefinitely.

Country in [[Southeast Asia]], also called East Timor, occupying the eastern half of the island of [[Timor]], with the Oecusse exclave and the islands of Atauro and Jaco. Its capital is Dili. A Portuguese colony until 1975, it was annexed by [[Indonesia]] after an Indonesian invasion, and Indonesian rule was marked by torture and massacres. In 1999 an act of self-determination sponsored by the United Nations led Indonesia to relinquish control. On May 20, 2002, Timor-Leste became the first new [[Sovereign state|sovereign state]] of the 21st century. It has a semi-presidential system and joined [[ASEAN]] in 2025. The economy depends heavily on [[Natural resource|natural resources]], especially oil, and on foreign aid. Its official languages are [[Portuguese language|Portuguese]] and Tetun, and most people are Roman Catholic.

Relatively shallow sea of the [[Indian Ocean]] between the island of [[Timor]] and northern [[Australia]], covering about 610,000 sq km. The Sunda Trench marks its deepest point, more than 3,300 m down. Lying on the [[Ring of Fire]], the sea is prone to earthquakes and tsunamis north of the trench and can be struck by major [[Cyclone|cyclones]] because of its proximity to the [[Equator]]. It contains significant [[Hydrocarbon|hydrocarbon]] reserves, and disputes over them led to the Timor Sea Treaty. The sea also has reefs and uninhabited islands. It was hit by the worst oil spill in 25 years in 2009. Australia's first inhabitants may have crossed it from the [[Malay Archipelago]] when sea levels were lower.

[[Island]] at the southern end of Maritime [[Southeast Asia]], divided between [[Indonesia]] and [[Timor-Leste]]. It lies at the eastern end of the [[Lesser Sunda Islands]], and its name derives from the Malay word for "east." Mainland [[Australia]] is less than 500 km away across the [[Timor Sea]]. The island covers 30,777 sq km and has a population of over 3 million. The Dutch and Portuguese divided it by treaty in 1859. Indonesia annexed East Timor in 1975 and regarded it as the country's 27th province, a claim never recognized by the United Nations or Portugal. Japanese occupation during [[World War II]] caused the deaths of between 40,000 and 70,000 Timorese.

American domestic terrorist and [[Gulf War]] veteran. McVeigh carried out the [[Oklahoma City bombing]] on April 19, 1995, destroying one-third of the Alfred P. Murrah Federal Building and killing 168 people, including 19 children. It remains the deadliest act of domestic terrorism in U.S. history. He sought revenge against the federal government for the 1992 Ruby Ridge incident and the 1993 [[Waco siege]]. He was convicted in 1997 on all counts and sentenced to death. He refused to pursue appeals and was executed by [[Lethal injection]] on June 11, 2001, the first federal inmate executed since 1963.

Late medieval Turco-Mongol, culturally Persianate Muslim empire (1370–1507). It was founded by [[Timur]] (r. 1370–1405), also called Tamerlane, who saw himself as the restorer of the [[Mongol Empire]] of [[Genghis Khan]]. At its height it dominated [[Iran]], Iraq, Afghanistan and much of [[Central Asia]]. Under Shahrukh Mirza and his son [[Ulugh Beg]], an astronomer and mathematician, the empire saw a Timurid Renaissance. After the dynasty lost most of Persia to the [[Aq Qoyunlu]], it survived in smaller states until Uzbeks under Shaybani Khan conquered almost all of them by 1507. Babur, a Timurid prince, used his kingdom in Afghanistan as a base to invade the Delhi Sultanate in 1526 and established the [[Mughal Empire]].

Soft, silvery-white [[Metal|metal]] with the symbol Sn and atomic number 50. Tin is a post-transition metal in group 14 of the [[Periodic table]], obtained chiefly from the [[Mineral|mineral]] cassiterite. It is malleable and bends by hand, producing a "tin cry" from the twinning of its crystals. Tin has the largest number of stable [[Isotope|isotopes]] in the periodic table, 10 in all. The first large-scale alloy was [[Bronze]], made with copper as early as 3000 BC. [[Pewter]], an alloy of 85–90% tin, has been used for flatware since the Bronze Age. Inorganic tin has low toxicity and resists [[Corrosion]], so tin-plated steel is widely used for food packaging, as "tin cans."

American actress, comedian, writer and producer. Fey began with the [[Chicago]]-based improv group The Second City, then joined [[Saturday Night Live]] in 1997 as a writer and performer. She created and starred in the [[NBC]] sitcom *30 Rock* (2006–2013) and later created the [[Netflix]] series *Unbreakable Kimmy Schmidt*. She acted in and wrote the film *Mean Girls* (2004). Her memoir *Bossypants* (2011) topped the best-seller list of [[The New York Times]] for five weeks. Fey has received ten Primetime Emmy Awards.

Singer, songwriter and actress, dubbed the "Queen of Rock 'n' Roll." Turner rose to prominence in the 1960s as lead vocalist of the R&B duo Ike & Tina Turner. After separating from Ike Turner in 1976, she launched a solo career, and her 1984 album *Private Dancer* produced "What's Love Got to Do with It," which won the [[Grammy Awards|Grammy Award]] for Record of the Year. She is one of the best-selling music artists of all time, with sales of over 100 million records. In 1967 she became the first Black artist and the first woman on the cover of [[Rolling Stone]].

Family of nine genera of ground-dwelling [[Bird|birds]] native to Mexico, Central America and [[South America]]. Tinamous are the only living palaeognaths able to fly, though they prefer hiding or running away from danger. Recent work places them among the ratites, most closely related to the extinct [[Moa]] of New Zealand. Males usually hold a territory and nest, which a succession of females visits to lay glossy eggs; the males incubate them. Tinamous live in habitats ranging from semi-arid alpine [[Grassland]]s to [[Tropical rainforest]]s. Their predators include [[Jaguar]]s and [[Vampire bat]]s, and habitat destruction is their main threat, with seven species listed as vulnerable. They have never been successfully domesticated.

Perception of ringing or other sounds with no corresponding external source. The word comes from [[Latin]] *tinnire*, "to ring." It affects about 10–15% of people, but only 1–2% find it a severe problem. Tinnitus is a symptom rather than a disease, most often caused by hearing damage or age-related [[Hearing loss|hearing loss]], and it can also result from ear infections or [[Brain tumor|brain tumors]]. Diagnosis rests on the patient's description and an audiogram, with [[Magnetic resonance imaging]] used if other problems are suspected. No drug treats it; management relies on sound generators, hearing aids and counseling.

American former actress and animal rescue advocate. [[Alfred Hitchcock]] discovered Hedren while she appeared in a television commercial in 1961, and cast her in *The Birds* (1963) and *Marnie* (1964). She later appeared in [[Charlie Chaplin]]'s final film, *A Countess from Hong Kong* (1967). Her commitment to animal rescue began in Africa in 1969, and in 1983 she founded the Roar Foundation, which supports the Shambala Preserve in Acton, California. She has alleged persistent sexual advances by Hitchcock, an account some biographers dispute.

Sultan of [[Mysore]] (1782–1799), known as the Tiger of Mysore. He succeeded his father, [[Hyder Ali]], and was a pioneer of [[Rocket|rocket]] artillery, expanding the iron-cased Mysorean rockets used against British forces in the Anglo-Mysore Wars. He commissioned the military manual *Fathul Mujahidin* and introduced a new coinage, a calendar and a land revenue system that initiated growth of the Mysore [[Silk|silk]] industry. He was killed on May 4, 1799, while defending Seringapatam against a combined force of [[East India Company]] troops, Marathas and the Nizam of Hyderabad. His religious policies remain contested: accounts of forced conversions and temple destruction in Malabar and Coorg contrast with portrayals of him as a tolerant ruler.

Italian dessert of [[Coffee|coffee]]-soaked ladyfingers (savoiardi) covered with a cream of egg yolks, [[Sugar|sugar]], mascarpone and cocoa powder. It originated in northeastern [[Italy]], and modern versions were popularized in restaurants from the 1970s. The name comes from the Italian *tirami su*, meaning "pick me up." Its origin is disputed, but obituaries say the modern version was invented at Le Beccherie, a restaurant in Treviso, on December 24, 1969, and added to the menu in 1972. Variations often incorporate [[Rum|rum]] or Marsala.

Capital and largest city of [[Albania]], located in the center of the country. The site has been inhabited since the [[Iron Age]] and was annexed by the [[Roman Empire]] after the Illyrian Wars. Tirana was founded in 1614 by the Ottoman Albanian nobleman Sylejman Pasha Bargjini. It remained unimportant until the 20th century, when the Congress of Lushnjë made it the capital. Today it is the country's economic, financial and political center, and it hosts the government and parliament. It is among the wettest and sunniest cities in [[Europe]].

Ring-shaped component surrounding a [[Wheel|wheel's]] rim, spelled tyre in Commonwealth English. A tire transfers a vehicle's load from the [[Axle]] to the ground and provides [[Friction|traction]]. Most modern tires are pneumatic, with a tread for traction and a body that holds compressed air. They are made from synthetic and [[Natural rubber|natural rubber]], fabric and wire, along with carbon black. Early tires were metal bands fitted to wooden wheels, and [[Locomotive|locomotives]] still use metal tires. Pneumatic tires are used on cars, [[Bicycle|bicycles]], motorcycles, buses, trucks and [[Aircraft]]. Unmaintained tires can cause flat tires and blowouts, and waste tires release toxic chemicals if they are not properly recycled. Regular use also produces microplastic particles containing those chemicals.

Group of similar cells and their extracellular matrix, from the same embryonic origin, that performs a specific function. Tissues lie between cells and [[Organ (biology)|organs]], which are formed by grouping several tissues. The word derives from the French *tissu*, "fabric." The study of tissues is called histology; Xavier Bichat is considered its father. In plants, tissues fall into three systems: the [[Epidermis (botany)|epidermis]], [[Ground tissue]] and [[Vascular tissue]]. Meristematic tissue, found at growing tips, consists of actively dividing cells that increase a plant's length and thickness. Ground tissue makes nutrients by [[Photosynthesis]] and stores reserves. Animal tissues are classified as epithelial, [[Connective tissue]], [[Muscle]] and [[Nervous tissue]].

Small, stocky woodland [[Passerine|passerine]] bird of the family Paridae, found mainly in the [[Northern Hemisphere]] and Africa. Eurasian and African members are called tits, while [[North America|North American]] species are called chickadees or titmice. The name titmouse is recorded from the 14th century and combines the Old English *mase* with *tit*, meaning something small. Tits are adaptable birds with short, stout bills and a mixed diet of seeds and insects, and many visit bird feeders near homes. After the corvids and [[Parrot|parrots]], they are among the most intelligent birds. They are territorial during the breeding season and often join mixed-species feeding flocks at other times.

Largest moon of [[Saturn]] and second largest in the [[Solar System]], after Jupiter's [[Ganymede (moon)|Ganymede]]. [[Christiaan Huygens]] discovered it in 1655. Titan is the only moon known to have a dense atmosphere, denser than Earth's, and the only known object besides Earth with stable bodies of surface liquid. Its atmosphere is mainly nitrogen and [[Methane]], forming hydrocarbon clouds and haze. The Cassini–Huygens mission, which arrived in 2004, revealed hydrocarbon lakes in the polar regions. At about 94 K (−179 °C), its [[Water cycle|methane cycle]] nearly resembles Earth's water cycle, and it is sometimes called the most Earth-like object in the Solar System.
